title: a neural manifest whose `vjp_exec` reference dangles (no enabled plugin provides it) is rejected in both languages, for different reasons
why: This manifest carries row01's golden descriptor inline: its block names
`vjp_exec.kernel` as `mlp_block_vjp`, but the manifest's plugin list only
enables `mlp_block_fwd`. The reference is dangling by construction — the
check that catches this is local to the manifest and fires before any
Both languages reject this fixture, but for different reasons, and that
difference is itself what this fixture checks. C++ has no consumer for
neural manifests yet, so both C++ registries refuse the manifest at
their existing pattern gate — 'recognized but not launchable by this
loader' — without ever looking at the blocks. Python's manifest loader is
the first neural-consuming loader, so it dispatches past the pattern
gate, validates every inline descriptor, builds the neural layer spec,
and only then hits the dangling-reference check, rejecting on
The Python rejection message is recorded here as the wording the first
C++ neural consumer must eventually match, once it exists.
Silently accepting this fixture in either language, or loading it as a
bare kernel without checking the exec reference against the enabled
plugin set, is exactly the failure mode this fixture exists to catch.
